topic: AP HC: insurer must pay accident compensation even if the policy was not moved to the new owner's name - Section 157 MV Act (Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance v. Purama Raghavamma)

slides.title: Bought a used vehicle? The **insurance** moves too
slides.subtitle: An insurer cannot refuse an accident claim just because the policy was still in the **old owner's** name.
slides.cite: **Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Purama Raghavamma & Ors.**, C.M.A. No. 486 of 2010 · Justice Balaji Medamalli

slides.label: The case
slides.title: A driver died at **work**
bullets: A tractor-trailer carrying sand for road work **overturned**, and its driver died.
The tractor had been **sold**. The buyer employed the driver, but the policy stayed in the **seller's** name.
His family claimed compensation. The Commissioner awarded **Rs 2,91,684**, payable jointly by the seller, the buyer and the insurer.

slides.label: Insurer's defence
slides.title: "Not our **customer**"
bullets: The insurance company appealed, saying the policy was **never transferred** to the new owner, so there was no cover.
It also raised points about the driving licence, passengers and late reporting of the accident.

slides.label: What the court held
slides.title: The policy goes with the **vehicle**
bullets: Under **Section 157(1)** of the Motor Vehicles Act, when a vehicle is sold, its policy is treated as **transferred** to the buyer.
So the policy was **valid** on the day of the accident. A name not updated is only a **technical** objection.
The insurer did not prove any breach of policy conditions. The appeal was **dismissed** and the award stands.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Still, update the **policy**
bullets: The law asks the buyer to apply to the insurer within **14 days** of the transfer to change the name on the policy.
This ruling protects **victims' families**. It does not mean you can skip the paperwork when you buy or sell.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

slides.title: Know the law, know your **rights**
lines: One important legal update every day, in simple words.
**Save** this, and **share** it with anyone buying a used vehicle.

caption:
Bought or sold a second-hand vehicle? Read this before an accident happens 🚜⚖️

A tractor-trailer carrying sand overturned and its driver died. The tractor had already been sold, but the insurance policy was still in the old owner's name. When the family claimed compensation, the insurance company said it had no customer and no cover.

The Andhra Pradesh High Court disagreed. Under Section 157(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, when a vehicle changes hands, its insurance policy is treated as transferred to the new owner. The policy was valid on the day of the accident, and a name not updated is only a technical objection that cannot defeat the family's claim. The award of Rs 2,91,684 was upheld.

Tip: the law still asks the buyer to apply to the insurer within 14 days of the transfer to update the name. Do it, so there is no dispute later.

Case: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Purama Raghavamma & Ors., C.M.A. No. 486 of 2010
Bench: Justice Balaji Medamalli, Andhra Pradesh High Court
